bias_targets.methodology: Annotating offensive Korean comments targeting gender groups (e.g., Women, Men, Feminists) and evaluating the F1 performance of sequence and token classification models (BERT, RoBERTa) on detecting these target categories and offensive spans.

Annotating offensive Korean comments targeting sexual minorities (e.g., LGBTQ+) and evaluating fine-tuned pre-trained language models for their ability to classify this target group and identify relevant text spans.

Categorizing hate speech targets by race, ethnicity, and nationality (e.g., Chinese, Korean-Chinese, Black, White, Southeast Asian) and measuring the classification and span prediction performance of Korean language models.
Identifying offensive language aimed at political affiliations (e.g., Progressive, Conservative) and benchmarking the target classification accuracy of contextual language models.
Evaluating models on their ability to detect offensive language targeted at religious identities (e.g., Muslim, Christian, Catholic, Buddhism) using a hierarchically annotated dataset.
Measuring the capability of multi-task and single-task learning models in detecting agism-related offensive comments within the Korean Offensive Language Dataset.
Annotating comments for offensive language targeting individuals based on socioeconomic status and testing language model detection performance.
Annotating offensive language targeting individuals based on disabilities or diseases (categorized under Miscellaneous target groups) to evaluate context-aware target detection models.
Evaluating text classification models on their capability to detect offensive language targeting physical appearance as defined in the dataset's detailed target group taxonomy.
